target_customer: Therapeutics companies and rare disease drug developers that pay for organoid based drug screening and safety work
problem: Standard disease models miss targets for rare and pediatric diseases. Rosebud screens drugs against organoids that carry patient gene mutations.
business_model: Fee for service organoid screening and partnerships, plus own rare disease discovery

founders.name: Kitch Wilson
prior_employers: Stanford (attending physician and molecular pathologist, 6 years)
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page. Schools for the degrees not stated.

founders.name: Evan Lyall
prior_employers: Contract data and ML engineer for startups
education: PhD, studied neural coding of perception at UC Berkeley

technical_complexity.rationale: Growing reproducible patient mutation organoids and linking them to drug response needs deep wet lab expertise and scaling work.

defensibility.rationale: Protocols and screening data accumulate with each program, but organoid services exist at academic groups and contract research firms.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. In January 2026 Rosebud partnered with iXCells Biotechnologies, which adds Rosebud organoids to its iPSC platform.

market_need_then: Pediatric and rare diseases lack models and treatments, and the YC page says a fetal-like organoid model found a heart disease drug target that traditional models could not. This is a company claim.

branding.name_origin: Search snippets say it references the sled in Citizen Kane, symbolizing a childhood derailed by outside forces. Not confirmed from a page I opened.
branding.domain_note: The rosebudbiosciences.com site redirects to rosebudbiosci.com (observed November 2026).

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline Growing micro-organs to find new drugs

brand_strength.rationale: Soft memorable name with a story, but no press about the brand itself and little public awareness beyond partner press releases.

outcome_analysis: Rosebud was founded in 2020 by a Stanford pathologist and a neuroscience PhD, joined YC in Winter 2022, won an NSF grant of about $275K in 2023 and announced a partnership with iXCells in January 2026. Venture funding is not verified, so the company looks capital efficient or quiet rather than failed.
notes: The company site redirected and was not fetched further. The NSF grant comes from a search result for HigherGov, with the grant period ended 7/31/24. Extruct lists investors 10X Capital, Arvantis Group and Gaingels with no amounts, which is unverified. Getlatka says no outside funding, an automated estimate. Hubrecht Organoid Technology as a rival appears only on an undated aggregator, so the competitor list is empty. No shutdown or layoffs found; status Active.
